# GSCG Content Framework — data-backed short-form video playbook

_Last researched: 2026-10-27. Built for Gonzaga Sport Consulting Group (~440 Instagram followers, ~1,200 LinkedIn followers)._

Machine-readable companion: [`framework.json`](./framework.json) (loaded by the studio app).

## How to read this

- Every number is linked to where it came from. If there is no link, it is **not a statistic**. It is a craft recommendation (marked _practitioner heuristic_).
- **Evidence grades** used throughout:
  - **[A] Platform-official.** Meta/Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn or TikTok help pages and executive statements.
  - **[B] Large vendor dataset.** Socialinsider, Rival IQ/Quid, Metricool or Buffer, with millions of posts and a published method. These are still vendor-reported, and definitions differ by vendor.
  - **[C] Weak.** Sponsored, survey-only, small-sample, platform-commissioned marketing research, or a secondary blog repeating a claim.
- **Engagement rates are not comparable across vendors.** Rival IQ divides by **followers**. Socialinsider's TikTok and LinkedIn rates divide by **views or impressions**. Quid's higher-ed TikTok rate divides by **views** ([Quid methodology](https://www.quid.com/knowledge-hub/resource-library/blog/2025-higher-education-social-media-engagement-report)). Compare GSCG only against a benchmark that uses the same denominator.

---

## 1. Ten things that matter most for GSCG

1. **Instagram ranks on watch time, likes and sends, in that rough order of emphasis.** Sends (DM shares) matter more for reaching non-followers. Mosseri, Jan 2025 [A] ([Social Media Today](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/)). The KPIs to track are **average watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach**.
2. **45–60 s is the strongest Reel length band** in a 9.77M-Reel sample: 0.35% ER and 10,374 median views. Reels **over 3 min** drop to 0.15% and are not placed in the Reels tab [B] ([Socialinsider](https://socialinsider.io/blog/instagram-reels-length/)).
3. **Realistic baseline for a 1–5K Instagram account:** about 580 views per Reel, about 3 comments and about 1 save [B] ([Socialinsider IG benchmarks](https://www.socialinsider.io/instagram-benchmarks)). At GSCG's size, carousels averaged more views (993) than Reels in the same table.
4. **Carousels slightly beat Reels on Instagram ER.** Carousels averaged 0.55% against 0.52% for Reels [B] ([Socialinsider](https://www.socialinsider.io/instagram-benchmarks)), and Rival IQ's 2025 report says "carousels outperformed Reels" [B] ([Rival IQ 2025](https://www.rivaliq.com/blog/social-media-industry-benchmark-report/)). Video is not automatically the best format, so pair each Reel with a carousel version.
5. **Higher ed is a top-engagement industry, and short video leads it.** Athletics-themed short video had an 11.80% median ER. TikTok athletics posts reached 13.59% (by views) against 5.89% on Instagram [B] ([Quid 2025 Higher Ed](https://www.quid.com/knowledge-hub/resource-library/blog/2025-higher-education-social-media-engagement-report)). Schools that leaned into TikTok and student-led storytelling "jumped 100+ places."
6. **LinkedIn video is growing, but documents and multi-image posts engage more.** Video ER by impressions was 6.00%, native documents 7.00% and multi-image 6.45% (2025) [B] ([Socialinsider LinkedIn](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin)). LinkedIn video viewership grew **36% YoY** [A, via LinkedIn rep] ([Digiday](https://digiday.com/marketing/linkedins-video-push-appears-to-be-working-in-2025/)).
7. **LinkedIn's own guidance:** awareness video should run **15–30 s** and deeper content **under 2 min**. Use **1:1 or 9:16**, hook in the **first 3 s** and add captions [A] ([Social Media Today, Apr 2025](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedin-shares-video-creation-tips/744933/)).
8. **Captions are mandatory.** **69%** of US consumers watch video with sound off in public, and **80%** of respondents said they're more likely to finish a video when captions are available. This comes from a Verizon Media/Publicis survey of 5,616 adults in 2019 [C, survey, older] ([3Play Media summary](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/verizon-media-and-publicis-media-find-viewers-want-captions/)).
9. **GSCG's Instagram is probably a business account, so it may not get the licensed music library.** Use **Meta's Sound Collection** (14,000+ royalty-free tracks) [A] ([Instagram Help](https://help.instagram.com/ipad-app/402084904469945)). On YouTube, Shorts over 1 min with **any** Content ID claim are **blocked globally** [A] ([YouTube Help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en)).
10. **Consistency beats bursts.** Moving from 1–2 to **3–5 posts/week** on Instagram gave about a 12% reach-per-post lift and more than doubled follower growth (2M+ posts) [B] ([Buffer](https://buffer.com/resources/how-often-to-post-on-instagram/)).

---

## 2. Platform playbooks

### 2.1 Instagram Reels (`reels`)

| Captions | Add captions or subtitles. Video autoplays muted in the feed. | [A] same. Muted autoplay per [QuickFrame](https://quickframe.mountain.com/blog/linkedin-video-ad-specs) [C] |
| Growth | Video viewership +36% YoY. Video creation is growing 2× faster than other formats. | [A, via [Digiday](https://digiday.com/marketing/linkedins-video-push-appears-to-be-working-in-2025/)] |
| Engagement | Videos get 1.4× more engagement than other posts (LinkedIn data shared with Axios) | [A/C, platform-reported] [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2025/02/04/linkedin-video-update-tiktok-alternative) |
| ER by format (by impressions, 2025) | Document 7.00%, multi-image 6.45%, **video 6.00%**, image 5.30%, text 4.50%, poll 4.20%, link 3.25% | [B] [Socialinsider LinkedIn](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin) |
| Platform trend | Interactions +99% YoY, clicks +122% (Sept 2023–Sept 2024) | [B] [Metricool 2025 study](https://metricool.com/social-media-study-2025/) |
| Best day | Wednesday, then Thursday and Friday (4.8M posts) | [B] [Buffer](https://buffer.com/resources/best-time-to-post-on-social-media) |
| Branding | A logo visible in the first 2 s gave a +17% CTR lift (LinkedIn Creative Lab, ads) | [C, secondhand] [Storykit](https://storykit.io/blog/linkedin-video-ads-best-practices) |

**Notes.**
- **4:5** is a feed-safe compromise between LinkedIn's square and vertical recommendations. This is a _practitioner heuristic_: LinkedIn names 1:1 and 9:16, not 4:5.
- Use **16:9 (`linkedin-wide`)** only for interview or testimonial footage shot landscape, or for content also going to long-form YouTube.
- On LinkedIn the audience is recruiters, alumni and client staff. Lead with **outcome or credibility** ("We presented to the Mariners front office"), not vibes.

### 2.5 Long-form YouTube (`youtube`)

| Spec | Value | Source / grade |
|---|---|---|
| Aspect | 16:9 | Platform standard |
| Length | Engagement is roughly flat between 1 and 5 min and drops significantly over 5 min (Wistia, all hosted video) | [B] [Wistia 2024 State of Video](https://wistia.com/blog/insights-state-of-video-report) |
| Hook | YouTube's retention report shows the share still watching at **30 s**. A vendor target is **≥60%** at 30 s, with strong hooks above 65%. | [C, vendor] [vidIQ](https://vidiq.com/blog/post/increase-audience-retention-youtube/) |
| GSCG use | Semester recap films, full client-trip vlogs, panel or speaker recordings, and case-competition walkthroughs. **3–8 min.** Chapter the video and cut 3–5 Shorts from it. | _Practitioner heuristic_ |

## 3. Format playbooks

Each format maps to an `id` in `framework.json`. Beats are in seconds for a **Reels default length**. Scale them proportionally for other platforms.

### 3.1 Day in the life (`day-in-the-life`)
**What it is:** A timestamped run through one member's day: class, client call, practice deck, event.
**Use for:** Recruiting season, member-life content and "what does GSCG actually do."
**Length:** Reels 30–60 s. LinkedIn 30–60 s. Shorts 30–45 s.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 0–2 | Face plus the on-screen promise: "A day as a sports consultant at Gonzaga." |
| Morning / context | 2–10 | 3–4 quick clips with timestamps such as "8:00 AM". |
| Core work | 10–35 | Client call, whiteboard, deck. This is the proof-of-substance beat. |
| Payoff | 35–50 | The best moment of the day (presentation, stadium, team dinner). |
| CTA | 50–60 | "Applications open [date]. Link in bio." |

**Hooks:** "POV: you consult for the Mariners as an undergrad". "What a consulting club day actually looks like". "6 AM to 10 PM as a GSCG analyst".
**Text:** Timestamps on every scene change. Burned-in captions on any voice.
**Music:** Lo-fi or upbeat bed from Sound Collection at about −18 dB under voice.
**KPIs:** Average watch time, sends per reach, profile visits.
**Evidence:** Watch time is a top Instagram ranking signal ([Mosseri](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/)) [A]. Schools using student-led storytelling rose 100+ places ([Quid](https://www.quid.com/knowledge-hub/resource-library/blog/2025-higher-education-social-media-engagement-report)) [B]. **No direct dataset isolates "day in the life" performance. The format choice is a heuristic.**

### 3.2 Come with me / POV (`come-with-me`)
**What it is:** First-person "come with me to…" video following one person through a single event or moment, with a voiceover or text narration.
**Use for:** Member spotlights, a first client visit, a stadium tour.
**Length:** Reels 15–45 s. LinkedIn 30–45 s.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 0–2 | "Come with me to present to the Seahawks". Start already moving, with no intro card. |
| Journey | 2–15 | Walking shots, badge, arena exterior. Cut every 1–2 s. |
| Arrival / peak | 15–30 | The room, the field, the handshake. |
| Reflection | 30–40 | One line on what they learned. |
| CTA / tag | 40–45 | Tag the member and the client (with permission). |

**Hooks:** "Come with me to…". "POV: your first client meeting is at T-Mobile Park". "Things I didn't expect at…".
**Text:** Large, top-third, at most 6–8 words per card.
**Music:** Sound Collection track with a beat drop timed to the arrival beat.
**KPIs:** Hook retention (3 s), completion, sends.
**Evidence:** Real-person "TikTok First" style drove ~3.3× more actions ([TikTok Creative Codes](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/library/Creative_Codes_ENG.pdf)) [C]. **No dataset isolates POV performance.**

### 3.3 Hype recap / montage (`hype-recap`)
**What it is:** A fast-cut highlight reel set to music: trips, case comps, kickoff and semester impact.
**Use for:** `client-trip-recap`, `hype-teaser`, `case-competition`, `semester-kickoff`, `impact-recap`.
**Length:** Reels 15–30 s. Shorts 15–30 s. LinkedIn 30–60 s, with stat cards and captions. YouTube 2–5 min (full recap).

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Cold open | 0–2 | The single best shot (stadium wide, group cheer). No logo. |
| Build | 2–10 | Cuts on the beat. Every shot under 1.5 s. |
| Proof cards | 10–20 | 2–3 stat or text cards: "3 clients · 40 members · 1 Mariners pitch". |
| Peak | 20–27 | Best group moment on the beat drop. |
| End card | 27–30 | Logo, plus a handle tag for the client and "Apply / Follow". |

**Hooks:** Start mid-action. A number: "We consulted for 3 pro teams this semester". "Spring '26 in 30 seconds".
**Text:** Stats must be **verified numbers only**. Keep text in the safe zone.
**Music:** This format depends most on music, but business accounts must use Sound Collection on Instagram ([Instagram Help](https://help.instagram.com/ipad-app/402084904469945)) [A]. For Shorts over 60 s, use the YouTube Audio Library only ([YouTube Help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en)) [A].
**KPIs:** Sends per reach (people tag friends who went), likes per reach, completion.
**Evidence:** Short video drove the most higher-ed engagement, with an 11.80% median on athletics content ([Quid](https://www.quid.com/knowledge-hub/resource-library/blog/2025-higher-education-social-media-engagement-report)) [B]. Sends weigh more for reaching non-followers ([Mosseri](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/)) [A]. **Cut-frequency numbers are a practitioner heuristic. No dataset found.**

### 3.4 Behind the scenes (`behind-the-scenes`)
**What it is:** Unpolished process footage: deck building, a networking room, prep the night before.
**Use for:** `networking-event`, `behind-the-scenes`.
**Length:** Reels 15–40 s. LinkedIn 30–60 s.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 0–2 | "What goes into a pro-team pitch" or "11 PM before the Blazers presentation". |
| Process | 2–20 | Real work: laptop screens (no client-confidential data), whiteboards, rehearsal. |
| Turn | 20–30 | The moment it comes together. |
| Close | 30–40 | Result or lesson, plus a CTA. |

**Text:** Labels that explain the jargon ("market sizing", "fan survey").
**Music:** A quiet bed, or natural sound with captions.
**KPIs:** Saves, comments, average watch time.
**Evidence:** Consumers say brands should provide original, human-centric content, and a third find trend-chasing embarrassing ([Sprout Social Index 2025](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/press/the-days-of-trend-chasing-are-over-new-research-from-sprout-social-reveals-a-third-of-consumers-think-jumping-on-viral-trends-is-embarrassing-for-brands/)) [B, survey]. Originality is favored in recommendations ([Mosseri](https://www.tubefilter.com/2022/04/21/instagram-adam-mosseri-algorithm-change-original-content/)) [A]. **No dataset proves BTS outperforms other formats.**

### 3.5 Testimonial / talking head (`testimonial`)
**What it is:** A member, alum or client contact on camera answering a single question.
**Use for:** `testimonial`, plus alumni outcomes.
**Length:** Reels 20–45 s. LinkedIn 30–90 s (the strongest LinkedIn fit). YouTube full interview.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Hook quote | 0–3 | Open on the strongest sentence, not "Hi, I'm…". |
| Lower third | 3–6 | Name, role, class year, client. |
| Story | 6–30 | One story with one specific detail. Use B-roll every 3–5 s to cover jump cuts. |
| Outcome | 30–40 | Internship, skill or offer. |
| CTA | 40–45 | "Join us: apply by [date]." |

**Text:** Captions are **mandatory**. Highlight 1–2 keywords per line.
**Music:** Low bed or none. Voice clarity first, because LinkedIn warns that poor audio "will immediately lose credibility" ([LinkedIn via SMT](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedin-shares-video-creation-tips/744933/)) [A].
**KPIs:** Average watch time, LinkedIn reactions and comments per impression, profile and page follows.
**Evidence:** 69% of people watch video sound-off in public ([Verizon/Publicis](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/verizon-media-and-publicis-media-find-viewers-want-captions/)) [C]. Prospective students say they most want testimonials from real students and career outcomes ([Campus Technology, sponsored](https://campustechnology.com/articles/sponsored-content/202608-beyond-the-feed-how-higher-ed-turns-social-media-into-a-measurable-enrollment-engine.aspx)) [C, sponsored].

### 3.6 Announcement / reveal (`announcement`)
**What it is:** A motion-graphic reveal: a new client, the exec board, a new partnership.
**Use for:** `client-announcement`, `exec-board-intro`.
**Length:** Reels 8–20 s. LinkedIn 10–30 s. Shorts 8–20 s.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Tease | 0–2 | "New client alert" or a silhouette or blurred logo. |
| Reveal | 2–6 | Client logo or person, timed to an audio hit. |
| Context | 6–14 | 1–2 cards: the project scope in plain language. |
| CTA / tag | 14–20 | Collab-post with the client if they approve. Tag on LinkedIn. |

**Text:** At most 3 cards, each readable in 2 s.
**Music:** A short riser into a hit (Sound Collection).
**KPIs:** Likes per reach, shares and reposts (on LinkedIn, client employees resharing), follower growth that day.
**Evidence:** Collab posts help the smaller account most ([Schöttl](https://hstalks.com/article/11245/download/)) [C]. Mosseri says likes matter slightly more for follower-facing content ([SMT](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/)) [A]. **Consider a carousel twin.** Carousels beat Reels on ER ([Socialinsider](https://www.socialinsider.io/instagram-benchmarks)) [B]. LinkedIn multi-image beats video (6.45% vs 6.00%) ([Socialinsider](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin)) [B].

### 3.7 Listicle / text-on-screen (`text-on-screen`)
**What it is:** B-roll under big sequential text: "3 things you'll do in GSCG", or a project spotlight in 4 facts.
**Use for:** `recruiting-apply`, `application-deadline`, `project-spotlight`, `org-overview`.
**Length:** Reels 15–30 s (match the read time). LinkedIn 20–45 s.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Hook headline | 0–2 | A numbered promise: "3 reasons to apply to GSCG". |
| Item 1 | 2–8 | One line, then a supporting clip. |
| Item 2 | 8–14 | Build to the strongest item last. |
| Item 3 | 14–22 | The strongest item, ideally a client name or outcome. |
| CTA | 22–30 | Deadline plus "link in bio", held at least 3 s. |

**Text rules:** Allow about 1 s per 3 words, in high-contrast type in the top-center third. Never put text where the UI sits.
**Music:** Upbeat Sound Collection bed. No voice needed.
**KPIs:** Saves (this content is reference material), link clicks and profile visits, completion.
**Evidence:** Designing for sound-off ([Verizon/Publicis](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/verizon-media-and-publicis-media-find-viewers-want-captions/)) [C]. **Save-driven formats should also exist as carousels and LinkedIn documents.** LinkedIn documents had the top ER at 7.00% ([Socialinsider](https://www.socialinsider.io/social-media-benchmarks/linkedin)) [B].

### 3.8 Trend / audio-driven (`trend-audio`)
**What it is:** A light, meme-native clip built on a trending format or sound.
**Use for:** `social-event`, `thank-you-holiday`.
**Length:** Reels 7–20 s. Shorts 7–20 s. **Do not post to LinkedIn**, or recut it as a warm thank-you with captions.

| Beat | Seconds | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | 0–2 | The trend's recognizable opening, with GSCG faces. |
| Twist | 2–10 | The GSCG-specific punchline. |
| Loop | 10–15 | End on a frame that flows back into the start. |

**Music:** **Risky for business accounts.** Trending licensed audio may be unavailable, ([Instagram Help](https://help.instagram.com/ipad-app/402084904469945)) [A], and vendor guides report boosted posts with library audio can get muted or rejected ([Fox Music](https://www.foximusic.com/blog/?p=587)) [C]. Prefer Sound Collection or original audio.
**KPIs:** Sends, rewatches (shown as average watch time above video length), reach to non-followers.
**Evidence:** A third of consumers find brand trend-chasing embarrassing ([Sprout 2025](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/press/the-days-of-trend-chasing-are-over-new-research-from-sprout-social-reveals-a-third-of-consumers-think-jumping-on-viral-trends-is-embarrassing-for-brands/)) [B, survey]. **Use sparingly, at about 1 in 8 posts.** The value of "looping" is a practitioner heuristic with no dataset found.

## 4. What drives views (evidence summary)

| Factor | What the evidence says | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| Watch time | A top-3 Instagram ranking signal | [A] [Mosseri](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/) |
| Sends / DM shares | A top-3 signal that weighs more for non-followers. Track sends per reach. | [A] same |
| Likes per reach | A top-3 signal that weighs more for followers | [A] same |
| Originality | Reposts and aggregators are demoted | [A] [Mosseri 2022](https://www.tubefilter.com/2022/04/21/instagram-adam-mosseri-algorithm-change-original-content/) |
| Length (IG) | 45–60 s is the best band. Over 3 min is excluded from the Reels tab. | [B] [Socialinsider](https://socialinsider.io/blog/instagram-reels-length/) |
| Length (contrary) | Emplifi finds longer brand Reels get more reach and views | [C, secondary] [PPC Land](https://ppc.land/instagram-reels-outperform-all-other-video-content-across-platforms-emplifi-research-finds) |
| Hook (first 2–3 s) | LinkedIn says hook in 3 s. TikTok decks say not to open with a logo card. | [A] [LinkedIn via SMT](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedin-shares-video-creation-tips/744933/). Precise hook-rate percentages online are **unsourced** [C]. |
| Captions | 69% watch sound-off in public. 80% are more likely to finish with captions. | [C, 2019 survey] [3Play](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/verizon-media-and-publicis-media-find-viewers-want-captions/) |
| Sound (TikTok) | 88% say sound is essential | [C, TikTok-commissioned] [TikTok/Kantar](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en-US/blog/kantar-report-how-brands-are-making-noise-and-driving-impact-with-sound-on-tiktok) |
| People on screen | Native, people-led ads drove 3.3× more actions | [C] [TikTok Creative Codes](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/library/Creative_Codes_ENG.pdf) |
| Collab posts | Higher reach than solo posts, but not additive. The smaller account benefits. | [C, n=100] [Schöttl](https://hstalks.com/article/11245/download/) |
| Posting frequency | 3–5/week gives about +12% reach/post vs 1–2/week, with diminishing returns above that | [B] [Buffer](https://buffer.com/resources/how-often-to-post-on-instagram/) |
| Posting time | LinkedIn: Wednesday is best. TikTok: Sunday mornings rank high. Instagram follows workday patterns. | [B] [Buffer](https://buffer.com/resources/best-time-to-post-on-social-media) |
| Cut pacing / faces in frame 1 / loops | **No reliable dataset found.** Treat these as craft heuristics and A/B test them on GSCG's own analytics. | — |

## 7. Known gaps (where the evidence is weak)
- No large-sample dataset was found for **cut frequency, faces in the first frame, or loop/rewatch effects**. Those guidelines are heuristics.
- Popular claims such as "63% of top ads deliver the message in 3 s" or "71% decide in 1.5 s" could **not be traced to a primary study** and are excluded.
- **No official LinkedIn sound-off percentage** was found. The 69% figure is a 2019 cross-platform survey.
- Rival IQ's exact 2025 Higher-Ed and Sports per-post numbers sit in the gated full report. Only qualitative findings and the theme medians above are confirmed.
- Vendor datasets are skewed toward brand accounts with 1K–1M followers. GSCG (440 IG) is at the bottom edge, so its own analytics will quickly become the better benchmark.
